summary.headline: JSW Infrastructure Q2 FY27 consolidated operating revenue rose 17% YoY to INR1,481 crore, but PAT fell to INR328 crore on forex loss and Fujairah shutdown.
summary.overview: Consolidated operating revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR1,481 crore (up 17% YoY) and operating EBITDA was INR674 crore (up 11%), while PAT declined to INR328 crore from INR369 crore. Port volumes grew only 2% YoY to 29.4 million tonnes, with the India business up 8% and Fujairah contributing nothing. Logistics EBITDA rose to INR81 crore from INR25 crore as the rake fleet grew from 42 to 78, and management cut the FY27 logistics margin guidance to 28% from 24% while keeping the INR400 crore EBITDA target. Management reiterated the consolidated FY27 EBITDA range of INR2,950-3,000 crore, though the port component was trimmed.

segments.name: Ports
segments.commentary: Q2 volumes 29.4 Mt (+2% YoY); India ops +8%, third-party volumes 45% of total. Fujairah contributed nil volume and an EBITDA loss of about INR16 crore in H1; port EBITDA margin fell to 49.4% from 53.1%.

segments.name: Logistics
segments.commentary: Domestic cargo 459,000 MT (+16% YoY); EXIM 88,000 TEUs (+12%). EBITDA INR81 crore (3.3x YoY). H1 logistics EBITDA was about INR153 crore; FY27 logistics margin guidance raised to 28% from 24% after accounting change netting haulage.

segments.name: Fujairah (international)
segments.commentary: Zero volume contribution in Q2. Eight tanks under commissioning with final FOIS permission expected around 29 October, with operations targeted for early November, but storage demand has fallen sharply.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated EBITDA target of about INR2,950-3,000 crore: port EBITDA now expected at INR2,550-2,560 crore against earlier INR2,600 crore; logistics EBITDA slightly above INR400 crore.
FY27 logistics EBITDA margin guidance revised to 28% from 24%; FY28 logistics margin guidance unchanged for now, with a revision to be considered in Q3 or Q4.

Rake fleet to rise from 78 to 110 by March 2027 (6 more to be operational in Nov-Dec; 32 more to be delivered in H2). Longer-term rake plan of around 267-270 (157 container, 110 LSFTO) is fluid and may rise.
FY27 capex expected at INR5,000-6,000 crore; overall FY27-28 capex guidance of INR16,500 crore retained. Cumulative capex about INR8,250 crore plus INR6,000 crore committed.
Port capacity target of 300 Mtpa by FY28 and 400 Mtpa by FY30 unchanged. Oman, Murbe work expected to start Q4 FY27; Keni awaits environment clearance (3-4 months more).
Q3 volume: H2 domestic cargo growth expected at 8-10% YoY; Jaigarh plus Dharamtar expected to handle about 46 Mt in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What was rail rake revenue in Q2 and H1, and what is the margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the overall logistics EBITDA margin is around 28% and the rake business margin around 90%, since only premium and rebate are booked as revenue with haulage netted off. Vishesh Pachnanda pointed to a logistics revenue of about INR279 crore, of which Navkar revenue was INR223 crore, with the balance being rail freight.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income rise sharply QoQ, and how is H1 capex tracking versus FY27 plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income rose due to interest on QIP proceeds. H1 FY27 capex was about INR2,100 crore against expected FY27 spend of INR5,000-6,000 crore; committed capex including INR6,000 crore of orders takes the total to about INR14,250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Ports EBITDA margins suppressed beyond Fujairah?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said terminal volumes carry 30-35% margins, and a dip at Jaigarh lowered the overall margin; a Jaigarh pickup is expected in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Fujairah status and when can volumes resume?
qa_highlights.answer: Eight tanks are in commissioning, with FOIS final permission expected around 29 October and operations targeted for the first week of November. Management flagged that storage demand in the area has fallen substantially because ships are not calling.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on Oman, Murbe and Keni, and are there delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Oman tenders were floated with bids expected mid-November and work to start in Q4 FY27; Murbe land acquisition is underway with work also expected Q4 FY27. Keni has been delayed on environment clearance: KCZMA recommended the proposal to MoEFCC, with 3-4 months more expected for EC.

qa_highlights.question: Can Jatadhar expand beyond 30 Mt and what is the cargo start timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Jatadhar has about 3.5 km of waterfront permission with 690 m in current development for 30 Mt; EC covers 52 Mt, and management sees potential to 100-120 Mt with more machinery. Cargo handling is expected to start around end-March 2027 or April 2027, with Cape-size facilities in Q3 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was logistics revenue guidance cut and can FY27 logistics targets be met?
qa_highlights.answer: The revenue cut reflects netting off haulage, while the EBITDA target of INR400 crore is kept; the rakes added by Q2 end give full H2 availability, which management said gives confidence. FY28 logistics margin guidance is unchanged for now, with a review in Q3 or Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA bridge and how are Jaigarh LPG delays explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Port EBITDA is now expected at INR2,550-2,560 crore against INR2,600 crore earlier, with logistics slightly above INR400 crore, for a total of INR2,950-3,000 crore. Jaigarh LPG marine works start by March 2027, while tankage was delayed by a change in planning authority and is now approved, with tanks around Q3 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What were Fujairah EBITDA contributions and what is the insurance claim status?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 FY26 Fujairah EBITDA was about INR134 crore and full-year FY26 about INR250 crore; H1 FY27 showed a loss of about INR16 crore. Insurance claims are still under assessment, pending a state declaration on whether the event is a war.

capex_capacity: Cumulative capex about INR8,250 crore up to September 2026, including INR1,500 crore spent in Q2; H1 FY27 capex about INR2,100 crore.
FY27 capex expected at INR5,000-6,000 crore; FY27-28 capex guidance of INR16,500 crore retained, with about INR6,000 crore committed via orders and about INR950 crore outstanding capex creditors.

Port capacity target of 186 Mtpa currently, 300 Mtpa by FY28 and 400 Mtpa by FY30. Oman tender bids due mid-November, work expected to start Q4 FY27; Murbe land acquisition and tenders done, work expected Q4 FY27; Keni awaits EC, 3-4 months more.

Slurry pipeline about 88% complete (257 km lowered, 10 km HDD in progress), commissioning on schedule by March 2027. Jatadhar berths ready for cargo by March 2027 (Panamax), Cape-size facilities Q3 FY28; Jatadhar EC covers 52 Mt, 690 m waterfront supports 30 Mt in phase 1.

Rake fleet 78 now, 72 operational since October, 6 more in Nov-Dec, 32 more in H2 to reach 110 by March 2027. Long-term rake plan of around 267-270 (157 container, 110 LSFTO) described as fluid and likely to rise.

Jaigarh LPG: marine operations by March 2027; tankage delayed by change in planning authority, now approved, with 2 large tanks expected by around Q3 FY28. Dharamtar mechanisation to complete Q4 FY27; Jaigarh mechanisation Q1 FY28. Kolkata OCT (13 Mtpa) concession signed; Kolkata interim operations at 6.3 Mtpa terminal began in Q2.
demand_pricing: Q2 port volumes 29.4 Mt (+2% YoY); India operations +8% in Q2 and +10% in H1; third-party volumes 45% of total in Q2 and third-party in India +13% YoY in Q2.
Q2 domestic logistics cargo 459,000 MT (+16% YoY); EXIM 88,000 TEUs (+12% YoY); H1 domestic cargo +26% YoY and EXIM +7% YoY.
Port revenue INR1,202 crore (+9% YoY), port EBITDA margin 49.4% vs 53.1%, attributed to Fujairah absence and lower-margin coal terminal volumes (Paradip Coal, Ennore Bulk, Mangalore, Tuticorin).
Paradip iron ore volumes fell after a 22 August vessel sinking off Paradip led to moisture-limit restrictions; about 8 lakh tonnes stock built up by end-September before shipments resumed.
H2 domestic cargo growth guided at 8-10% YoY; Jaigarh plus Dharamtar expected at about 46 Mt in FY27; Fujairah storage demand has fallen sharply as ships are not calling.

Logistics margin: rake business margin about 90% on premium and rebate only, with haulage netted off; FY27 logistics EBITDA margin guidance revised to 28% from 24%, EBITDA target INR400 crore retained.
risks_watch: Fujairah: 8 tanks targeted to start in early November, but storage demand has fallen sharply and operations may stay constrained; insurance claim pending.
FY27 EBITDA target of INR2,950-3,000 crore requires a steep H2 ramp in logistics with 32 rakes still to be delivered in H2 and 6 more in Nov-Dec.
Keni environment clearance expected in 3-4 months; Oman and Murbe work start in Q4 FY27 depends on bids and land acquisition; port capacity 300 Mtpa by FY28 at risk.
Jatadhar Cape-size facilities not until Q3 FY28; Jaigarh LPG tankage delayed; Jaigarh volumes soft in Q2.
Forex losses on rupee depreciation and higher finance cost and depreciation; finance cost in H2 may rise from ROU lease expense on rakes.
Q3 FY27 results: watch the FY28 logistics margin revision, the rake fleet progress against 110, and Paradip iron ore and Kolkata terminal volumes.
key_quotes: Despite these uncertainties, India's economic fundamentals remain strong, supported by robust domestic demand, continued investments in infrastructure, manufacturing-led growth and favorable policy initiatives.

In the short-term, in the immediate-term, the strategy is to get the 8 terminals, as I told you, which are currently under testing to get them official commissioning done and start operations by November 1st week.
Long-term prospects, extremely bullish, but immediate prospects, we have to wait and watch.
So from a logistics perspective, we are confident that we should be in a position to achieve slightly above INR400 crores in terms of EBITDA.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the India port and logistics ramp-up and on the FY27 EBITDA range, but cautious on Fujairah, describing the situation as fluid and the immediate demand outlook as wait-and-watch. Answers on Keni timing and Jaigarh tankage were direct about delays.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: Port capacity to 300 Mtpa by FY28
rows.why: Capacity goes from 186 Mtpa to 300 Mtpa, with about INR6,000 crore committed via orders, but Keni still awaits environment clearance (3-4 months more) and Oman and Murbe work starts only in Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Logistics margin reset to 28%
